question.problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(0,-3)$ and is parallel to the line passing through the points $(-5,1)$ and $(-1,-2).$
question.worked_solution:
Since parallel lines have equal slopes, both lines should have the same slope.

First, let's find the slope of the line passing through the points $(-5,1)$ and $(-1,-2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-2-1}{-1-(-5)} \\  & =\frac{-2-1}{-1+5} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we wish to find a line that has a slope of $-\frac{3}{4}$ and passes through the point $(0,-3).$ To find the equation of this line, we use point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-3) & =-\frac{3}{4}(x-0) \\ y+3 & =-\frac{3}{4}x \\ y & =-\frac{3}{4}x-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write this equation in standard form.

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{3}{4}x-3 \\ 4y+12 & =-3x \\ 3x+4y & =-12\end{aligned}
$$
